primitives.name: Idea Reproduction Cost
primitives.verbatim_quote: The important practical difference between discovery and creation relates to the matter, referred to in a previous chapter, of the cost of reproduction of ideas as compared with things.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_i': 'cost of reproducing an idea (dimensionless energy units)', 'C_m': 'cost of reproducing material goods (dimensionless energy units)'}
primitives.assumptions: Ideas are non-rivalrous and can be replicated at near-zero marginal cost.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When intellectual property protections prevent free copying, C_i approaches C_m.

layer2.mapping: Idea reproduction cost maps to information-theoretic entropy reduction in GSI's Bayesian update framework; in GSE, it governs transition probabilities between productive states.
layer2.telemetry: Rate of idea adoption across market segments and time.

primitives.name: Knowledge Extensibility
primitives.verbatim_quote: The knowledge of a fact may be extensible almost without cost throughout the membership of competitive society.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E_k': 'extensibility factor of knowledge (dimensionless)', 'N_s': 'number of societal participants (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Knowledge dissemination is frictionless within competitive networks.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When access is restricted or communication channels are degraded, E_k diminishes.

layer2.mapping: Extensibility underpins GSI’s probabilistic forecasting models; in GSE, it defines the scope of strategic adaptation.
layer2.telemetry: Network density of shared knowledge and cross-organizational learning velocity.

primitives.name: Curiosity Compensation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Moreover, the mere gratification of curiosity may be ample compensation for the effort required to get an idea, so that this cost can be entirely neglected or may even become negative.
primitives.assumptions: Curiosity-driven exploration yields utility exceeding direct effort cost.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When U_c < C_e, exploration ceases; when U_c > C_e, incentive increases.

layer2.mapping: Curiosity compensation functions as a reward signal in GSI’s reinforcement learning; in GSE, it influences exploratory behavior in state-space search.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of novel idea generation vs. resource allocation efficiency.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that ideas differ fundamentally from material goods in terms of reproduction cost. This leads to a dual structure: (1) the economic dynamics of idea propagation, where knowledge spreads with negligible marginal cost, and (2) the cognitive incentives driving discovery, particularly when curiosity provides intrinsic reward. These two aspects form a duality in how innovation is modeled—economically via extensibility and cognitively via utility maximization. The failure mode arises when either the assumption of low reproduction cost breaks down due to IP enforcement or when curiosity fails to provide sufficient utility to justify effort. In GSI, this manifests as a Bayesian model where prior beliefs about idea diffusion are updated based on observed extensibility patterns. In GSE, it translates into a dynamic system where productive states evolve according to the availability of new ideas and the cost of implementing them.
